properties.snippet: This map displays the Master Well Inventory records in Kansas along with index wells and High Plains aquifer analysis data. This map is maintained by the Kansas Geological Survey.
properties.description: This map shows data from the Kansas Master Groundwater Well Inventory (MWI), a central repository for the state's primary groundwater well datasets. The most "accurate" common source fields are used to represent the well sites. The MWI maintains the primary identification tags to link specific well records to the original data sources. This mapper is managed by the Kansas Geological Survey. For more information about the data, see the Groundwater Master Well Inventory page.

properties.snippet: WWC5 water wells in Kansas. Data is a compilation of multiple water well sources.
properties.description: The Water Well Completion Form Database (WWC5) contains information from records submitted by water well drillers to the Kansas Department of Health and Environment. Data is compiled by the Kansas Geological Survey. Drilling companies are mandated by state legislation under the Kansas Groundwater Exploration and Protection Act (KSA 82a-1201 et seq.) to provide information pertaining to the location, type, use, casing, nearest source of contamination, and so on of the well drilled using the WWC5 form. No water quality data is provided in this database. A good portion of the archived WWC5 records are in the form of electronically scanned images of the forms themselves. As such, the only standard database items entered into an Oracle RDBMS relate to the location information of the WWC5 wells, use of the well, when the well was completed, status of the wells, well depth, static water elevation, and the name of the drilling company servicing the site.

properties.snippet: This StoryMap explores water-focused field trips within Kansas. It's a compliation of places where students can discover, experiment, and connect with the water that shapes their world.
properties.description:
From streams and wetlands to reservoirs and nature centers, Kansas offers countless opportunities for students to explore how water shapes our landscapes, communities, and daily lives.

These field trips immerse students in real-world science—studying watersheds, observing aquatic life, and seeing firsthand how water connects people and place. Each stop in this story map highlights experiences that make learning about water not just educational, but unforgettable.

To visit more educational resources, visit the Kansas Water Office Education website: https://www.kwo.ks.gov/education

properties.snippet: This Hub application allows users to navigate the two main sections of the State Water Plan Fund (SWPF), and view the breakdown of each section and sources of revenue, along with a budget process breakdown. The SWPF is the statuatory fund created for the purpose of implementing the Kansas Water Plan.
properties.description:
The Kansas State Water Plan Fund was created in 1989 by the Kansas Legislature and is used for establishing and implementing water-related programs or projects identified in the Kansas Water Plan. This Hub page will allow users to navigate the two main sections of the State Water Plan Fund, and view the breakdown of each section and sources of revenue, along with a budget process breakdown.

Additional information regarding the background of the funds is located within the Hub application. To view the interative Kansas Water Plan page: https://kansas-water-plan-ksdot.hub.arcgis.com/ 
 
Kansas Water Office: https://kwo.ks.gov/

properties.snippet: The State Water Infrastructure Grant Program (previously the HB 2302 grant program) dashboard displays each fiscal year of the program. Including total awarded amount, total applicants that applied, and the amount each entity was awarded. It offers a breakdown of funded applicant program types and loan assistance types, as well as by county and regional planning area.
properties.description:
In 2023, Governor Laura Kelly and the Kansas Legislature, through Sen. Sub. for HB 2302, increased the amount of state funding for the State Water Plan Fund (SWPF). Its provisions included the creation of two new water-related grant funds: the Technical Assistance Grant Fund and the Water Projects Grant Fund.

The two grant funds serve to help identified Kansas entities to obtain the up-front technical assistance and the on-the-ground actions needed to address various water quantity and quality needs. The two funds are generally directed to supporting water-related infrastructure activities.
 
This application displays each fiscal year the program has been available. Including the total awarded amount, total applicants that applied, and the amount each entity was awarded. It also offers a breakdown of funded applicant program types and loan assistance types.  
 
More information, visit the KWO webpage: https://www.kwo.ks.gov/events-initiatives/grant-programs/state-water-infrastructure-grant-programs
